posts.title: The Far Side of the Body
posts.desc: Twenty-one conditions and abilities that separate pain, pleasure, sleep, memory and movement, with the evidence and its limits beside each case.

sections.text: Sections Pain Pleasure Control Sleep The uncanny mind The body remade Unusual abilities The comparison

sections.head: One gene, different kinds of pain
sections.text: Some changes to the SCN9A gene cause attacks of burning pain. Other changes leave a person unable to feel pain from birth. SCN9A encodes Nav1.7, a sodium channel involved in nerve signals. Certain variants make pain-sensing neurons more excitable; other variants prevent the channel from working. The effects depend on the particular mutation and how it is inherited. The diagram below compares distinct mutations, not stages that a person moves between. SCN9A GeneReviews Cox 2006 That comparison is a useful beginning. These conditions can separate things we normally experience together: recognizing a face and feeling it is familiar, moving a hand and feeling responsible for it, remembering a life and learning a new list. Some mechanisms are well established. Others rest on a few patients and competing explanations. The difference matters throughout this guide. Distinct changes to SCN9A Two effects of altered Nav1.7 channels, with different inheritance patterns. This compares mutation-specific effects. Erythromelalgia also has causes unrelated to SCN9A, and several other genes can cause congenital pain insensitivity. SCN9A GeneReviews Pain insensitivity GeneReviews One

sections.head: Complex regional pain syndrome
sections.text: Pain after an injury After an injury, a limb can develop continuing pain out of proportion to the original damage, with changes in temperature, color, swelling or movement. Touch that should be harmless may hurt. CRPS involves altered pain processing alongside other nervous-system and inflammatory changes. A clinic study of 39 patients found an association between suicidal thoughts, pain and depressive symptoms. It cannot establish a suicide rate for everyone with CRPS. Lee 2014

sections.head: Cluster headache
sections.text: Severe attacks around one eye Cluster headache produces recurring attacks of intense one-sided pain, often with a watering eye, a blocked nose and restless movement. In an online survey of 1,604 people meeting the study's cluster-headache criteria, the average recalled pain rating was 9.7 out of 10. The survey's case definition already required severe pain. Its rating describes respondents' experience, rather than an objective ranking of all pain: participation was voluntary, diagnoses were not independently confirmed, and other conditions were rated from memory. High-flow oxygen is an established treatment for attacks. Burish 2021 Oxygen trial, 2009

sections.head: Inherited erythromelalgia
sections.text: Burning, hot, red extremities Feet or hands become red and warm during attacks of burning pain, often triggered by heat or exercise. Some inherited cases come from gain-of-function SCN9A variants that make pain-sensing neurons easier to excite. Severity varies, even within a family, and the pain need not be constant. This is the first half of the gene comparison above. It explains one form of erythromelalgia, not every person with the condition. GeneReviews Two

sections.head: Ecstatic seizures
sections.text: Bliss as a seizure symptom A small number of people with focal epilepsy describe brief feelings of intense well-being, clarity or certainty during a seizure. In one clinical case published in 2013, electrical stimulation of the right anterior insula reproduced the patient's ecstatic sensation. That supports a role for this region in a wider seizure network. The reports are too few to establish a universal explanation for ecstatic experiences. Picard 2013 Clinical review

sections.head: Gourmand syndrome
sections.text: A new preoccupation with good food After a stroke, a political journalist became absorbed in dining and eventually changed from political reporting to food columns. His doctors used this and another case to investigate newly acquired eating interests. Their 1997 study identified 36 patients with gourmand syndrome; 34 had damage involving the right anterior brain, across several regions and causes. Many also had cognitive or behavioral difficulties. The eating interest was one part of a broader change. The series connects it with brain injury without showing that a particular lesion will produce it. Regard and Landis 1997

sections.head: Musical chills
sections.text: Frisson A passage of music can bring a shiver, goosebumps and intense pleasure. In a small imaging experiment, eight listeners selected for reliable musical chills showed PET changes consistent with dopamine release while hearing their chosen music. A separate fMRI analysis distinguished activity before the chills from activity at their peak. The study connects musical pleasure with reward processing, while separating the buildup from the peak. Its carefully selected listeners do not represent everyone who enjoys music. Salimpoor 2011 Optional: pressing for pleasure Classic brain-stimulation experiments made animals repeatedly work for stimulation. Some human patients also pressed stimulation buttons compulsively. But repeated pressing measures reinforcement: a strong drive to obtain something need not mean extraordinary enjoyment of it. Reviews distinguish wanting from liking, and question whether the famous human experiments demonstrated pure pleasure. Kringelbach and Berridge 2010 Three

sections.head: Fatal familial insomnia
sections.text: An inherited prion disease Despite the name, this is more than an inability to sleep. A disease-associated PRNP variant causes a fatal neurodegenerative illness involving abnormal prion protein, with severe sleep disruption, autonomic problems and progressive movement and cognitive changes. Damage is especially prominent in the thalamus. The course varies, and sleep medicines do not cure the underlying disease. Clinical overview

sections.head: Fear after amygdala damage
sections.text: The patient known as SM SM, a woman with bilateral amygdala damage from Urbach-Wiethe disease, reported little fear while handling snakes, visiting a haunted house or watching frightening films. Yet she and two other patients with similar damage experienced panic during a laboratory carbon-dioxide inhalation challenge. Their results complicate the idea that the amygdala is the single source of fear. Its damage can affect responses to external threats without abolishing fear arising from an internal bodily threat. Feinstein 2011 Feinstein 2013

sections.head: Lesch-Nyhan disease
sections.text: Compulsive self-injury with pain intact The severe form of an HPRT1-related disorder disrupts the recycling of purines, components of DNA and RNA. It causes excess uric acid and serious neurological difficulties, including involuntary movement and compulsive self-injury, most often in boys. A child may bite his lips or fingers while still feeling pain. This is not evidence that he wants to be hurt. Protective equipment, careful care and treatment of the broader disorder matter; punishment can make the behavior worse. HPRT1 GeneReviews Clinical overview Four

sections.head: REM sleep behavior disorder
sections.text: Moving during dreams During REM sleep, most skeletal muscles normally lose their tone. In RBD, this suppression is impaired, and people may shout, punch or act out dreams. Isolated RBD can precede a neurodegenerative disease. A specialist cohort of 1,280 patients produced an estimated 73.5 percent risk of developing parkinsonism or dementia by 12 years. This was a survival-analysis estimate, not a count showing that three quarters of all participants became ill: average follow-up was 3.6 years. The group was older and mostly male. Its result describes that diagnosed cohort, not every cause of dream movement or an individual's future. Postuma 2019

sections.head: Cataplexy
sections.text: Muscle weakness while awake Laughter or another strong emotion can bring sudden weakness: a jaw droops, knees buckle, or the whole body collapses. Consciousness is usually preserved, and attacks can last seconds to minutes. Cataplexy is closely associated with narcolepsy type 1 and the loss of neurons that produce orexin, a chemical involved in stabilizing wakefulness. The overlap with REM muscle suppression helps explain the symptom, though an attack is not simply the person falling asleep. Dauvilliers 2014

sections.head: Sleep paralysis
sections.text: Aware but unable to move Someone waking up or falling asleep can become aware while REM-associated muscle paralysis persists. They may be unable to move or speak, with frightening perceptions of an intruder, pressure on the chest or floating outside the body. Similar experiences recur in accounts from different cultures, though hallucinations do not accompany every episode. The overlap of waking awareness and sleep physiology explains much of the experience without determining how a person interprets it. Sharpless and Barber 2011 Optional: long sleep and sudden bangs Kleine-Levin syndrome causes recurring episodes of prolonged sleep, with changes such as confusion and altered behavior during an episode. People often return toward their usual function between episodes, although some have lasting difficulties. Miglis and Guilleminault 2014 Exploding head syndrome is different: a person perceives a sudden loud noise around a sleep transition, generally without pain. Clinical overview Five

sections.head: Cotard delusion
sections.text: Believing you are dead A person may believe they are dead, do not exist, or have lost their organs. One man with severe depression believed his brain had died while his body remained alive. A 2013 PET case study found reduced metabolism across parts of his frontal and parietal cortex compared with healthy controls. His EEG was normal, and he was awake and speaking. This was not a brain-death finding or a comparison with anesthesia. Depression, medication and the lack of a matched patient group limit what this single scan can explain about Cotard delusion. Charland-Verville 2013

sections.head: Capgras delusion
sections.text: A familiar person seems an impostor Someone believes a loved one has been replaced by an identical impostor. In a 1997 case study, a man with a head injury recognized his parents' photographs but lacked the usual difference in skin-conductance response between familiar and unfamiliar faces. He accepted his parents' identity over the telephone. The authors proposed disrupted links between visual recognition and emotional familiarity, alongside problems evaluating the resulting belief. It is a plausible explanation for that patient's pattern, not proof of a severed wire in every case. Hirstein and Ramachandran 1997

sections.head: Alien hand syndrome
sections.text: Movement without a sense of control A hand may grasp objects or interfere with what the other hand is doing, without the person intending the action. Sometimes the hand also feels unfamiliar or unowned. Different forms occur after damage to frontal, parietal or callosal regions, including after stroke. These cases help distinguish making a movement from experiencing agency over it. The different injury patterns also show why no single broken connection explains every case. Panikkath 2014 Optional: visions after sight loss Charles Bonnet syndrome involves visual hallucinations in people with impaired vision. They may see figures, animals or patterned scenes, often while recognizing that the images are not real. Its reported frequency varies across populations and diagnostic definitions. Clinical overview Six

sections.head: Bone where it should not grow
sections.text: Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva FOP causes extra bone to form in soft connective tissues, including muscles, tendons and ligaments. It can bridge joints and restrict movement. Disease-associated ACVR1 variants alter bone-forming signals; episodes can occur spontaneously or after injury. Unnecessary biopsies, operations and intramuscular injections can provoke further bone formation, so care must account for that risk. Characteristic malformed great toes are often present at birth, before extra bone develops. GeneReviews

sections.head: Blue skin from altered hemoglobin
sections.text: Hereditary methemoglobinemia A Kentucky family helped make inherited methemoglobinemia famous. In one form, variants in both copies of CYB5R3 reduce an enzyme's ability to restore oxidized hemoglobin. The resulting methemoglobin cannot carry oxygen normally and can make skin appear blue. The type confined mainly to red blood cells differs from a more severe form affecting other tissues. Methylene blue can lower methemoglobin in suitable patients; it does not repair the inherited defect and can be dangerous with G6PD deficiency. Cawein 1964 Expert recommendations, 2021

sections.head: Progeria
sections.text: Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome The classic form comes from a particular LMNA variant that produces progerin, an abnormal form of a protein supporting the cell nucleus. Children develop growth failure, loss of body fat and hair, joint stiffness and serious cardiovascular disease. Intellectual development is usually normal. Some features resemble aging, but the condition is not a complete accelerated version of ordinary life: its pattern of disease is specific, and it does not reproduce every illness of old age. GeneReviews Optional: Julia Pastrana Pastrana, a singer and dancer with hypertrichosis and enlarged gums, was exhibited for her appearance. After her death in 1860, her husband and manager had her body embalmed and continued displaying it. In 2012, a Norwegian research-ethics committee recommended return and burial of her remains, while acknowledging that her own wishes were unknown. Her story belongs here as a history of how a person was treated, rather than as another unusual body to inspect. Committee statement Seven

sections.head: Congenital insensitivity to pain
sections.text: SCN9A loss of function Loss-of-function variants in both copies of SCN9A can prevent pain sensation from birth. Touch and other abilities may remain intact, but loss of smell is characteristic. Without pain's warning, unnoticed burns, injuries and joint damage become serious hazards. Other genes cause different forms of congenital pain insensitivity, sometimes with additional impairments. The original 2006 report identified SCN9A mutations in affected people from three Pakistani families. Cox 2006 GeneReviews These genetic findings made Nav1.7 a target for pain research. A recent drug milestone concerns another channel. Suzetrigine, sold as Journavx and approved in the US in 2025 for moderate to severe acute pain in adults, selectively blocks Nav1.8. It is not an approved SCN9A/Nav1.7 drug. FDA label

sections.head: Highly superior autobiographical memory
sections.text: Remembering dates and personal events People with HSAM can retrieve unusually detailed memories tied to dates in their own lives. In a 2012 study of 11 selected participants, they named the weekday for randomly chosen past dates correctly about 97 percent of the time, compared with about 15 percent for controls. They also recalled personal events, with some checked against records. Performance on many standard laboratory memory tasks was ordinary. The ability is specific, and neither that study nor its results establish perfect recall of every day, every detail or every kind of information. LePort 2012

sections.head: Human echolocation
sections.text: Learning to interpret echoes Some blind people use tongue clicks and their echoes to judge objects and navigate. In a 2011 experiment with two expert echolocators, recorded echoes activated parts of the brain usually associated with vision. The small study showed how these experts processed echoes, rather than how every blind person would. A later study trained 12 blind and 14 sighted adults over 20 sessions in ten weeks. Both groups improved on echolocation tasks. The ability can be learned, with practice and improvement measured in specific tasks. Thaler 2011 Norman 2021 Optional: a reported scent of Parkinson's Joy Milne's reported ability to recognize an odor associated with Parkinson's helped motivate a study of skin sebum. The researchers found candidate chemical markers that differed between their patient and control samples. These are candidate markers requiring validation, rather than a clinical screening test. Her report of noticing an odor before diagnosis was retrospective. Trivedi 2019 What the cases show

sections.head: Abilities can come apart
sections.text: Rare conditions can expose distinctions that everyday experience conceals. But a memorable patient, a mutation's effect in a cell and a long-term cohort answer different questions. A case can suggest a mechanism. Establishing how widely it applies takes further evidence. Support in a crisis If you're struggling or worried about someone, the US 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline offers support by call or text at any hour. Further reading

sections.head: Sources and kinds of evidence
sections.text: Sources include original studies, clinical references and official documents. Case reports describe particular people; experiments test narrower questions; cohort estimates depend on who was enrolled and followed. Clinical reviews put those findings in context. Open the grouped source list
Start here

sections.head: How to use this guide
sections.text: This guide helps you recognize a problem, find the relevant care advice and prepare a question for your clinician. The main route gives a short answer for each subject. Open a chapter's reference for the studies, tables, tools and less common situations. Start with when to get help . Then choose the first days , feeding , sleep , illness , safety or your own health . The contents rail filters chapter names and topics; it does not search every word. A page cannot examine a baby. Most advice here assumes a healthy, full-term infant. Prematurity, illness and a prescribed care plan can change it. Call your clinician when feeding, breathing, growth or behavior concerns you. Use your local emergency number for an immediate threat. US guidance is the default. National schedules and policy differences are identified in the reference. Historical charts retain their stated dates. Evidence labels are editorial descriptions, not formal evidence grades. Models, estimates and illustrative diagrams are labeled beside the figure. I am not a doctor. This reference was assembled with AI assistance from the linked guidance and research. It is a way to find sources and questions, and it needs clinical judgment and current local guidance. For prematurity, a diagnosis, adoption, multiples or other circumstances, go to your situation . The source note explains what the review can and cannot establish. Tools: symptom card · medicine chart · rehydration plan · growth plot · vaccine timeline · visit schedules . When to get help now

sections.head: Emergency: when to get help now
sections.text: If the baby is not breathing normally, cannot wake, is blue on the lips or tongue, or is having a seizure, call emergency services. A young infant with fever needs immediate assessment even when they look well. This card helps you act while you contact a clinician. Call 911 (or 999 / 112) now if your baby is not breathing, is gasping, or turns blue or gray on the lips, tongue, or face (central blue color, not just dusky hands and feet) is choking and cannot cry, cough, or breathe (start back blows and chest thrusts, below, while help is coming) is limp, floppy, or will not wake up is having a seizure (rhythmic jerking, stiffening, staring and unresponsive) has heavy bleeding you cannot stop, a serious fall onto a hard surface, or a suspected poisoning with collapse Be seen immediately (emergency department, or call your doctor now) if your baby is under 3 months old with a rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher. In a young infant this is an emergency on its own, even if the baby looks well AAP 2021 NICE NG143 is working hard to breathe: fast breathing, grunting with each breath, nostrils flaring, or the skin pulling in at the ribs or neck will not feed, has far fewer wet diapers, no tears, a sunken soft spot, and is hard to rouse (signs of dehydration) has a rash of small red or purple spots that do not fade when you press a glass against them (the non-blanching or glass test) Meningitis Now has a bulging, tense soft spot, a high-pitched or inconsolable cry, or a stiff neck vomits green or bloody fluid, or has forceful projectile vomiting after most feeds runs cold instead of hot: a temperature below 36.0C (96.8F) in a newborn Call your doctor today (same day, non-urgent) if your baby has a fever and is 3 to 6 months old, or has had any fever for more than about 3 days is feeding noticeably less, is much more sleepy or fussy than usual, or just seems not themselves has diarrhea or vomiting that is not settling, ear-tugging with fever, or a worsening cough When in doubt: a nurse advice line (in the US, your pediatrician's after-hours line; NHS 111 in the UK; healthdirect 1800 022 222 in Australia) can help you decide. Trust a worsening pattern over a single number.

sections.head: For the birthing parent: your own warning signs
sections.text: Pregnancy-related problems can appear after discharge. Know the warning signs for the whole year after birth, and tell the person assessing you that you recently had a baby. CDC Hear Her Call 911 if you have chest pain, or trouble breathing or shortness of breath a seizure an urge or plan to harm yourself or the baby, inability to keep either of you safe, or hallucinations, delusions or confusion Call your provider now if you have bleeding that soaks one or more pads in an hour, or clots larger than an egg CDC warning signs a fever of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher a headache that will not ease with medicine, or that comes with vision changes a swollen, red, warm, painful leg, or a c-section or tear incision that is not healing Seek immediate medical care for these warning signs. If you cannot reach your provider, go to an emergency department. Tell the team that you gave birth within the past year. CDC Hear Her warning-sign poster AWHONN POST-BIRTH warning signs

sections.head: Numbers to have ready
sections.text: Emergency: 911 (US) · 999 (UK) · 112 (EU and many others) Poison Help (US) : 1-800-222-1222 · or webPOISONCONTROL.org Swallowed-battery hotline (US) : 1-800-498-8666 National Maternal Mental Health Hotline (US, call or text) : 1-833-852-6262 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline (US, call or text) : 988 · Postpartum Support International : 1-800-944-4773 My pediatrician: · After-hours line: · Nearest ER: Tip: print this section (it expands for print) and put it on the fridge with the blanks filled in.

sections.head: Two first-aid sequences worth knowing cold
sections.text: If a baby is choking (awake, cannot cry or breathe) Lay the baby face down along your forearm, head lower than chest, and give up to 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades with the heel of your hand. Turn the baby face up, keeping the head lower than the chest, and give up to 5 chest thrusts with the heel of one hand on the breastbone. This is the 2025 AHA technique; it replaces the older two-finger method. AHA 2025 Repeat back blows and chest thrusts. Have someone call 911. If the baby becomes unresponsive, start infant CPR. AHA / AAP 2025 . Take a hands-on infant CPR class; reading is not the same as practice. If a baby swallows a button battery Go to the emergency department immediately ; serious esophageal burns can occur in as little as two hours. Call 1-800-498-8666 . Poison Center battery guideline If the child is at least twelve months old , can swallow, and may have swallowed a lithium coin-cell battery within the past twelve hours , give 10 mL (two teaspoons) of honey every ten minutes, up to six doses, while traveling to care. Do not delay emergency care to obtain honey. Poison Center guideline Do not give honey under 12 months (botulism risk), and do not make the child vomit. National Capital Poison Center A swallowed button battery can cause serious esophageal burns in as little as two hours. Seek emergency assessment immediately. Poison Center guideline Raimond Spekking / Wikimedia, CC BY-SA 4.0 · · · The on-ramp

sections.head: Before the baby
sections.text: the third trimester Prepare the few things that have deadlines. Choose a clinician and ask how to reach them after hours. Arrange a firm, flat infant sleep space and, if you will travel by car, a correctly installed rear-facing seat. Confirm leave, insurance enrollment and practical help before the birth. Ask the birth team about vitamin K, newborn screening, hepatitis B and your local eye-prophylaxis policy. You can buy most clothes and accessories later. Leave and insurance deadlines · Newborn care decisions Reference: before the baby You do not need a finished nursery. Somewhere safe to sleep, a place to change a diaper, and a few clothes is plenty. Photo: Kaboompics / Pexels Choosing a pediatrician Preparing the car seat Cord-blood banking Newborn care choices Leave, insurance, and the boring paperwork Preparing for discharge and the first week

sections.head: Choosing a pediatrician
sections.text: Choose a practice before the birth if you can. Ask how newborn follow-up is arranged, who answers overnight, whether the office accepts your insurance, and where a sick young infant is assessed. Tell the practice about a planned home birth or a likely NICU stay. A prenatal meeting can help you decide whether you can ask questions comfortably; it cannot predict every future encounter.

sections.head: Preparing the car seat
sections.text: Have the rear-facing seat installed before discharge. Follow both the seat and vehicle manuals, including the allowed recline and installation method. Keep a child rear-facing until the seat’s rear-facing height or weight limit is reached. A certified technician can check the installation with you. Avoid bulky clothing under the harness, and use only accessories the seat manufacturer approves. NHTSA seat guidance .

sections.head: Cord-blood banking
sections.text: If cord-blood banking is being considered, discuss it before delivery with the maternity team. Ask whether public donation is available, what collection requires, and whether a known family condition gives directed banking a medical purpose. Private storage is a paid service; a list of possible future treatments is not evidence that this baby’s stored cells will be useful. Do not change a clinical birth plan on the strength of a bank’s advertising.

sections.head: Newborn care choices
sections.text: Ask the birth team about vitamin K, infection prevention, newborn screening and feeding support while there is time to discuss them. Have the maternal hepatitis B result available at delivery. These decisions have different purposes and timing, so declining one is not a reason to skip the others. The first-days section separates them, and the team can explain local policy and any baby-specific exceptions.

sections.head: Leave, insurance, and the boring paperwork
sections.text: Ask the employer and insurer what must be filed, by whom and by what date. US Marketplace birth enrollment generally has a sixty-day window; employment-based plans have their own special-enrollment procedures. Confirm the baby’s effective coverage date and keep copies of submissions. Federal FMLA offers unpaid, job-protected leave only to eligible workers with covered employers. State benefits and employer pay policies require separate checks. Marketplace enrollment ; FMLA eligibility .

sections.head: Preparing for discharge and the first week
sections.text: Pack what the place of birth asks for, identification and medicines, a way to get home, and a few changes of clothes. At home, start with a safe sleep space, feeding supplies suited to the plan, diapers, a thermometer and basic clothes. Arrange practical help with food and household tasks. A registry can wait; a number to call when feeding is going badly is useful immediately. The first hours and days

sections.head: The first hours and days
sections.text: birth to day 3 Watch feeding, weight, temperature and jaundice. Newborns need frequent feeds and early follow-up. Breastfed babies usually feed 8 to 12 times in 24 hours. Ask the team when to wake your baby, how to judge milk transfer and when the first weight and jaundice check will happen. A little early weight loss is common; continued loss, poor feeding, low diaper output or increasing jaundice needs assessment. A percentage alone cannot show that a baby is adequately fed. CDC newborn feeding Early weight and feeding · Jaundice and when to call Reference: the first hours and days Before discharge, confirm feeding, screening results and the next appointment. kenan zhang / Pexels Vitamin K, hepatitis B and other newborn care The three newborn screens: heel-prick, heart, and hearing Newborn appearance and symptoms Early weight loss and feeding assessment Jaundice and the bilirubin check Is the baby getting enough in the first days? Circumcision The first night

sections.head: Vitamin K, hepatitis B and other newborn care
sections.text: Vitamin K given after birth helps prevent serious bleeding; the injection is recommended even for babies who look well. Hepatitis B protection depends on maternal test status, birth weight and clinical stability. For positive maternal status, CDC specifies vaccine and hepatitis B immune globulin (HBIG) within twelve hours. Unknown status also requires vaccine within twelve hours; the birth team must apply the weight- and test-specific HBIG rules. For a stable infant at least 2,000 g whose mother tests negative, CDC schedule notes specify a birth dose within twenty-four hours. Confirm the actual plan with the birth team. Eye prophylaxis and cord management are separate parts of newborn care. CDC vitamin K ; CDC hepatitis B notes .

sections.head: The three newborn screens: heel-prick, heart, and hearing
sections.text: US newborn screening includes blood spots, a pulse-oximetry check for certain critical heart conditions, and hearing screening. Screening can miss a condition and a result needing follow-up is not itself a diagnosis. Timing, repeat tests and the bloodspot panel vary by programme and clinical circumstances. Ask who receives each result, when to expect it, and what follow-up is booked. Do not assume silence means a normal bloodspot result. HRSA screening process .

sections.head: Newborn appearance and symptoms
sections.text: Newborn appearance changes quickly, and a photograph cannot reliably distinguish a harmless variation from illness. Ask the team to explain a rash, swelling, unusual movement or breathing that worries you before discharge. Blue lips or tongue, difficulty breathing, a baby who is hard to wake, and poor feeding need prompt assessment. A temperature of 38°C (100.4°F) or above in a baby under three months needs immediate medical attention; it is not the upper end of a normal newborn range. Use actual age since birth for this fever rule. NICE fever guidance .

sections.head: Early weight loss and feeding assessment
sections.text: Compare weight with birth weight and the feeding assessment, not with a chart alone. The NEWT figure uses published cohort medians, not clinical percentile curves. It cannot show that a baby is hydrated or transferring enough milk. Ten percent weight loss requires assessment, and concerning feeding or urine output warrants help before that point. Ask when the next weight check is due and who will review it. Original NEWT study ; AAP newborn assessment . On a small screen, swipe charts sideways to see the full plot. With a keyboard, focus a chart and use the arrow keys. Selected estimated median weight-loss anchors from the original NEWT study of exclusively breastfed infants born at least thirty-six weeks in Northern California hospitals, 2009 to 2013. Lines interpolate the listed points; this is not the official percentile tool or a clinical threshold chart. Flaherman 2015

sections.head: Jaundice and the bilirubin check
sections.text: Bilirubin interpretation depends on age in hours, gestational age and clinical risk factors. Skin colour alone cannot establish the level or treatment threshold. Before discharge, get the measured result, follow-up time and contact number. Jaundice in the first day, worsening jaundice with poor feeding or unusual sleepiness, and pale stools need prompt clinical attention. Do not use sunlight as treatment. The clinician decides whether another measurement, feeding help or phototherapy is needed. CPS guideline ; AAP jaundice advice .

sections.head: Is the baby getting enough in the first days?
sections.text: Watch the baby as well as the clock: feeding frequency, swallowing, weight change and diapers belong together. Breastfed newborns commonly feed eight to twelve times in twenty-four hours. By day five, fewer than six wet diapers, continuing weight loss or difficulty feeding calls for help. These are assessment signs, not a formula for deciding that intake must be adequate. Record what is happening and seek feeding support promptly. CDC newborn feeding .

sections.head: Circumcision
sections.text: Circumcision is an elective decision for many families and a medical recommendation in some individual circumstances. Ask about possible benefits, risks, pain relief, aftercare and how urgent problems are handled. If you choose it, have the procedure and pain control arranged through a qualified clinician. CPS parent information .

sections.head: The first night
sections.text: Use the feeding and follow-up plan you were given. Keep a separate sleep space ready beside the bed and ask for help before fatigue makes holding the baby unsafe. If you might fall asleep during a feed, avoid a sofa or armchair. Return the baby to their own sleep surface when the feed ends or when you wake. AAP safe-sleep guidance . The fourth trimester

sections.head: The early weeks
sections.text: week 0 to 6 Expect interruptions, and arrange a break. Sleep and feeding rarely settle on a timetable. Crying often increases in the early weeks, but an average curve cannot explain a new, painful or unusual cry. Feed, change, hold and check temperature; call if your baby seems ill or will not feed. If frustration builds, put the baby on their back in an empty crib and step away briefly while you get help. Never shake a baby. Low mood that is severe or lasts beyond two weeks deserves a clinical conversation. Crying and colic · Mood after the birth Reference: the early weeks Feeding, sleep and crying can change through the early weeks. There is no promised six-week turning point. Vidal Balielo Jr. / Pexels Crying in the early weeks Soothing and colic When frustration builds Low mood after birth Unwanted thoughts and urgent mental-health symptoms Your body, your identity, your relationship Follow-up after birth

sections.head: Crying in the early weeks
sections.text: Crying often increases in the early weeks, but a population average is not a diagnosis. A change in crying, a baby who seems unwell, or concern about feeding deserves assessment. The crying chapter explains the reported averages without inventing an individual normal range. Do not wait for a promised six-week turn if something seems wrong.

sections.head: Soothing and colic
sections.text: Try feeding if hungry, a diaper change, holding, gentle movement or a quieter room. A technique that helps one evening may not help the next. Persistent distress needs a feeding and health assessment before it becomes a shopping list of remedies. The colic section distinguishes limited evidence from allergy-directed care.

sections.head: When frustration builds
sections.text: If frustration builds, put the baby on their back in an empty crib, step away briefly and call someone who can take over. Never shake a baby. Tell regular caregivers the same plan before a difficult evening. If you fear you may hurt the baby, arrange immediate help rather than staying alone with them. AAP abusive head trauma report .

sections.head: Low mood after birth
sections.text: Mild, short-lived mood changes in the first two weeks are often called baby blues. Severe symptoms, difficulty functioning, or symptoms that persist need assessment; two weeks is not a waiting requirement. Tell your clinician if you cannot sleep even when someone else cares for the baby, feel persistently hopeless, or struggle to care for yourself. See caregiver mental health for treatment and emergency routes. NIMH guidance .

sections.head: Unwanted thoughts and urgent mental-health symptoms
sections.text: Unwanted frightening thoughts can be distressing. Describe them to a qualified clinician, including whether there is an urge, intention or plan to act and whether you can keep yourself and the baby safe. Hallucinations, delusions, mania or marked confusion after birth require emergency help. If anyone is in immediate danger, call emergency services and have another safe adult care for the baby. This distinction needs assessment, not reassurance from a checklist. NIMH perinatal guidance .

sections.head: Your body, your identity, your relationship
sections.text: Tell the care team about pain, bleeding, trouble passing urine or stool, feeding pain and exhaustion. Ask what recovery should look like after your particular birth and which changes require urgent care. Share household work explicitly: who washes bottles, makes meals and answers the next waking. A plan can change as feeding and recovery change.

sections.head: Follow-up after birth
sections.text: Postpartum care may need several contacts rather than a single six-week appointment. Confirm the next contact, how to get help between visits, and follow-up for pregnancy complications or mental-health symptoms. The urgent warning signs still apply after an apparently uncomplicated birth and after the routine appointment. Seek care when a symptom occurs. CDC warning signs . Feeding

sections.head: Feeding
sections.text: the whole year Feed the baby, and check that feeding is working. Breast milk, iron-fortified infant formula, or a combination can meet a healthy infant's needs. Look at swallowing, diaper output and growth together. Painful feeds, a sleepy baby who cannot feed, or poor weight gain needs help with the feed itself. Prepare formula with the exact water-to-powder ratio; do not dilute it. Around six months, when developmentally ready, add iron-rich foods and safe textures while milk remains the main food. Discuss early peanut introduction with a clinician if your baby has severe eczema or egg allergy. CDC formula preparation Formula preparation · Solids and allergens Reference: feeding Bottle markings help measure a feed. Growth, swallowing and diapers provide more context. Photo: Burst / Pexels Breastfeeding evidence Checking intake Latch, intake and pain Milk storage, medicines and feeding pain Preparing and choosing formula Starting solids and introducing allergens Food safety and choking Vitamin D and iron

sections.head: Breastfeeding evidence
sections.text: Breastfeeding can provide nutrition and infection protection, and families need practical support when they choose it. The size of a reported benefit depends on the outcome and study design. Observational comparisons can also reflect differences in income, health and access to care; an odds ratio is not a percentage reduction in every baby’s risk. The survey figure below describes feeding rates, not why a family stopped. Feed the baby adequately and use the approach that can be sustained with appropriate care. CDC breastfeeding guidance . US breastfeeding measures for infants born in 2022. “Any” and “exclusive” are different measures, calculated among all infants. CDC NIS-Child Parents report feeding histories in the survey. These percentages do not identify why a family stopped or estimate the effect of a leave policy.

posts.title: The Number: How Much Would You Need to Retire?
posts.desc: Estimate a retirement savings target from spending, then test how income, debt and returns affect the saving schedule. A working calculator, withdrawal research and 2026 US tax examples, with the assumptions beside them.

sections.text: A $1 million portfolio gives you a $40,000 first-year withdrawal at 4%. That is the useful part of the retirement rule. It does not tell you whether $40,000 covers your life, whether the portfolio survives fifty years, or whether you can stop working today. This guide turns spending into a savings target, then shows how income, debt and returns change the time needed to reach it. The calculator is a simplified projection. The tax examples are for the United States, checked October 3, 2026. 01

sections.head: What the 4% rule tested
sections.text: A historical result for a particular portfolio and retirement length. William Bengen's 1994 study tested portfolios against past US stock, Treasury and inflation data. A first-year withdrawal of 4% of the starting balance, followed by inflation adjustments to that dollar amount, lasted at least thirty years in every start-year scenario he examined. His illustrative portfolio held half stocks and half intermediate-term Treasuries and was rebalanced annually. Bengen 1994 The distinction matters: on $1 million, the first withdrawal is $40,000. If inflation is 3%, the second is $41,200, whatever the portfolio is worth then. This is a spending rule that may consume principal, rather than a claim that investments earn a steady 4%. The later Trinity study tested different stock-and-bond mixes and payout periods. It excluded taxes and transaction costs. Cooley, Hubbard and Walz 1998 The arithmetic is simple: annual portfolio withdrawals divided by the initial withdrawal rate equal the starting portfolio target. At 4%, that is twenty-five times the amount you withdraw. A $40,000 withdrawal target needs $1 million; $100,000 needs $2.5 million. Include withdrawal taxes, insurance and irregular expenses in that budget. For a longer retirement, compare lower rates too. The calculator offers 3.5% and 3.25%, requiring about 28.6 and 30.8 times annual withdrawals. Those are scenarios to investigate, not guarantees for a fifty-year retirement. A lower rate cannot eliminate market risk. Bengen's later 4.7% result also has an allocation attached. His September 2025 research describes 55% stocks, 40% bonds and 5% cash as the book's baseline, then tests higher stock allocations. It does not justify taking 4.7% from a single stock fund. Bengen 2025 02

sections.head: What the target buys
sections.text: These are withdrawals before tax, rather than guaranteed investment income. Invested portfolio First-year withdrawal Monthly equivalent Budget to test $1,000,000 $40,000 $3,333 A lean budget in many places. Housing and healthcare may take much of it. $1,500,000 $60,000 $5,000 More room for recurring expenses, still dependent on housing and household size. $2,500,000 $100,000 $8,333 A larger budget, with taxes and exceptional expenses still to account for. $5,000,000 $200,000 $16,667 A high spending allowance. The withdrawal rule has the same limits. Calculated at a 4% initial withdrawal rate, with monthly figures rounded. At 3.5%, the same portfolios support smaller initial withdrawals. These targets count assets available to fund retirement. A house you plan to keep living in cannot also pay the grocery bill. The Federal Reserve measured median family net worth at $192,900 in its 2022 survey, including housing and other nonfinancial assets; median financial assets among families holding them were $39,000. Neither figure describes a retirement-ready portfolio. Fed SCF 2022, tables 2 and 3 03

sections.head: Estimate your number
sections.text: Change the assumptions and compare the resulting saving schedules.

sections.head: Your spending target and saving schedule
sections.text: Drag the sliders or type over the numbers. The model uses today's buying power and a constant return. It estimates accumulation only, with no simulation of retirement withdrawals or chance of success. Figures and reference data checked October 3, 2026. Take-home pay per year, after taxes $ US median $72,330 Spending living costs; exclude payments on the debt entered below, which the model pays separately $ /mo = $ /yr US average $6,545 Retirement withdrawals you want per year before withdrawal taxes; linked to current spending until you change it $ /yr withdraw $100K/year Investments and cash retirement funding only; exclude your home, car and emergency reserve $ 2022 median financial assets $39K Debt the balances you want the model to repay before new investing $ example $40K debt When you want it years from now; follows the projection until you change it yrs · 2054 Debt interest rate nominal APR; simplified monthly interest, with 3% inflation % Investment return per year, after inflation, investment taxes and fees % Initial withdrawal rate 4% rule · ×25 3.5% · ×28.6 3.25% · ×30.8 Load the reference example Available surplus 32% of take-home pay Portfolio target $1,110,000 25 × yearly spending Projected years 28 from today you reference example your number Model: monthly contributions and constant real returns, default 5%, chosen as an illustration. All surplus pays modeled debt first, then enters investments; existing investments stay invested. Debt APR is converted to today's dollars using assumed 3% inflation. Keep minimum payments affordable: this model does not reproduce a lender's repayment schedule. Income, spending and saving keep pace with inflation. The target excludes Social Security and pensions and has no retirement horizon. It is not a result of a withdrawal backtest. Reference example: $72,330 annual post-tax household income (2024 Census), $39,000 financial assets (2022 Fed median among holders), no debt, and an assumed 4.5% saving rate. This combination is synthetic, not a measured median household. The spending-track marker is $78,535 divided by twelve, the BLS 2024 average for consumer units; it includes categories such as pension contributions that differ from this tool's living-cost input. Census Fed BLS The gap between income and spending controls contributions. It also constrains what the calculator can tell you: a constant-return curve cannot show a layoff, a rent increase or a market crash. Try several returns and budgets before treating its date as useful. Calculated from zero, with no debt, constant 5% real annual returns, contributions at each year-end and a target of twenty-five times spending. These are model outputs, not typical American retirement dates. The interactive calculator instead uses monthly contributions. Saving half of take-home pay reaches that illustrative target in about seventeen years. That rate is feasible for some high-income households and unavailable to many others. Rent, caregiving, disability, debt and wages constrain the gap. Changing a slider is easier than changing those conditions. 04

sections.head: What gets taxed
sections.text: The account and the income type matter as much as the amount withdrawn. Consider two simplified 2026 examples. A single employee under 65, earning $100,000 with no pretax contributions or credits, owes $13,170 in federal income tax using the standard deduction, plus $7,650 in employee Social Security and Medicare taxes: $20,820 altogether. A married couple, both under 65, selling $120,000 of stock with a $60,000 cost basis can owe $0 in federal income tax if the shares were held over a year and they have no other income. Different filing statuses and income types make this a tax illustration, not a like-for-like retirement budget. IRS 2026 tables IRS payroll rates Only the $60,000 gain is income in that sale. The couple's $32,200 standard deduction leaves $27,800 of taxable income, within the 2026 married-joint 0% long-term capital-gains bracket of $98,900. With no other income, that deduction and bracket allow up to $131,100 of long-term stock gains at a zero federal income-tax rate. Ordinary income uses deduction and bracket space too. State taxes can still apply. IRS capital gains IRS 2026 limits

sections.head: Roth conversions need a withdrawal plan
sections.text: A Roth conversion moves pretax retirement money into a Roth account and generally includes it in that year's ordinary income. Low-income years may make conversion cheaper; unused deductions can sometimes cover the taxable amount. Conversions can also increase the tax on capital gains and reduce health-insurance subsidies. There is no universal tax-free conversion allowance. IRS Publication 590-A Before age 59½, a conversion ladder also needs money for the waiting period. Taxable converted amounts generally have a separate five-tax-year clock before withdrawal avoids the 10% early-distribution tax, unless an exception applies. Roth IRA ordering rules distribute regular contributions first, then conversions, then earnings. Tax-free earnings have another qualification test, generally requiring the Roth five-year period and age 59½. These clocks are easy to confuse. IRS Publication 590-B

sections.head: HSA receipts can stay useful
sections.text: An eligible health savings account can receive federally deductible contributions, grow without annual federal income tax, and reimburse qualified medical expenses tax-free. You can defer reimbursement without a time limit, but the expense must follow the HSA's establishment. Keep receipts; it must not have been reimbursed elsewhere or taken as an itemized deduction. State treatment can differ. IRS Publication 969 IRS Notice 2004-50, Q39 05

sections.head: Debt before the target
sections.text: A portfolio calculation is useful only after the monthly bills fit. The Moneylender and His Wife, Quentin Massys, 1514. Louvre, public domain . The Federal Reserve's 2025 household survey found that 63% of adults would cover a hypothetical $400 emergency entirely with cash, savings or a credit card paid off at the next statement. The other 37% is not a measure of everyone unable to pay; some would borrow or use another method. It does show why a long investment plan needs a short-term reserve. Fed SHED 2025 A $7,000 card balance at a 22% APR incurs about $128 of interest in its first month under a simple APR-divided-by-twelve calculation. Paying principal reduces that charge. Minimum-payment payoff times depend on the issuer's formula and future rates; a single twenty-two-year estimate cannot describe every card.

sections.head: A workable saving order
sections.text: Keep essential bills and minimum debt payments current, and build enough cash to avoid borrowing for the next ordinary surprise. Check an employer retirement match, its contribution limit and vesting rules. A match can be valuable, but it is plan-specific. Direct extra debt payments to the highest interest rate. Avoiding a 22% card charge is a much firmer benefit than hoping for a stock return. Build a reserve suited to your employment and obligations. Then choose retirement accounts according to eligibility, taxes, fees and the age when you need access. Automate investing in a diversified portfolio. A taxable account can help fund years before retirement-account access is straightforward. Fees belong in the return assumption. With no additional deposits, $100,000 compounding at 5% for forty years becomes about $704,000; at 4%, about $480,000. That calculated difference illustrates a one-percentage-point reduction in annual net return. Check both fund costs and advisory charges. SEC fee guide 06

sections.head: Income and time
sections.text: A raise helps only to the extent that it becomes additional saving. An extra $10,000 saved at each year-end for twenty-five years grows to about $632,000 at a constant 7% return. That is a calculated example before taxes and fees. A $10,000 gross raise produces less after tax, and the example is in nominal dollars unless 7% is explicitly a real return. Training or changing employers can improve the gap, but admission, tuition, physical demands and local openings matter. The following occupations offer routes that can avoid a bachelor's degree. Their median wages describe established workers, not new entrants. Occupation examples and entry requirements Path Annual median wage Entry and constraints Elevator mechanic $109,910 Typically a four-year apprenticeship with paid on-the-job training; most states require a license. Air traffic controller $148,080 FAA entry-level applicants must be under 31. Academy training is paid; medical, testing and experience requirements apply. Nuclear reactor operator $122,890 Extensive training, experience and an NRC license. Shift work and continuing examinations. Radiation therapist $105,310 Usually an associate or bachelor's degree; most states require licensing or certification. Registered nurse $97,550 Associate, bachelor's or approved diploma routes, plus licensure. Employers may prefer a bachelor's degree. Dental hygienist $98,100 Usually an associate degree; programs typically take three years. All states require licensing. Power-line installer $95,320 Technical instruction and on-the-job training; apprenticeships are common. Dangerous work and emergency callouts. Technology sales Check the offer Separate guaranteed base pay from commission at quota. A posted on-target figure is not assured income; education requirements vary. Military career Plan-specific pension Separate retirement eligibility and pay rules from current salary. Service obligations and retirement system determine the result. Military OneSource The seven wage figures are BLS May 2025 national medians, checked October 3, 2026. They are gross wages. Each occupation links to its pay and entry requirements; the FAA hiring page supplies the entry-level age and academy details. Checking electrical assemblies at Vega Aircraft, Burbank, June 1942. Color photograph by David Bransby. Library of Congress, public domain . Compounding also changes the contribution schedule. With $20,000 a year deposited monthly and a constant 7% effective annual return, the first $100,000 takes about 4.3 years. The step from $900,000 to $1 million takes about 1.2. These figures assume no taxes, fees or interruptions. A real market can delay either step. Calculated time for each $100,000 increment with monthly deposits totaling $20,000 a year and a constant 7% effective annual return, before taxes and fees. Dollars here are nominal. 07

sections.head: What the success stories show
sections.text: Documented wealth is evidence of an outcome, not of its probability. Large fortunes have been accumulated on ordinary salaries. The familiar stories often describe people investing into old age and leaving money at death, rather than funding decades of early retirement. They also omit the savers who bought unsuccessful companies. Four examples, with their limits Ronald Read , a gas-station attendant and janitor, left an estate worth nearly $8 million. Brattleboro Memorial Hospital described his long-held investments when naming a pavilion for him. BMH 2022 Grace Groner , an Abbott secretary, left more than $7 million to a foundation supporting Lake Forest College students. The college traces it to an initial $180 stock investment. That successful concentration in one employer is an outcome, not a diversification strategy. Lake Forest College 2010 Sylvia Bloom worked as a legal secretary for sixty-seven years and bought small amounts of stocks her employer bought. Henry Street Settlement's account describes her gift and the scholarship fund it created. Henry Street 2018 Anne Scheiber , a retired IRS employee, left $22 million for women's scholarships in 1995. The Associated Press reported the bequest; Yeshiva University describes the continuing fund. The often-repeated claim that the entire fortune began with only $5,000 is not needed to understand that gift. AP 1995 Yeshiva University 08

sections.head: How assets fund spending
sections.text: Withdrawal, yield and annuity payout are different quantities. A dividend is a payment from a company; a portfolio withdrawal may also involve selling shares. A bond ladder or annuity can return some of your original principal. Comparing their cash payments as if they were the same investment return makes the larger number look better than it is. Source What it does What to account for Diversified stock-and-bond portfolio Fund spending from dividends, interest and sales. A withdrawal rate sets a spending policy. Asset allocation and the order of returns affect how long it lasts. TIPS ladder Schedule inflation-linked Treasury principal and interest. Match maturities to spending. A ladder that spends principal ends on its final maturity; extending the horizon costs more. Selling early exposes you to market prices. TreasuryDirect Lifetime annuity Buy a contractual stream of payments. Quote the actual age, survivor option and inflation protection. A fixed nominal payment loses buying power; insurer solvency and limited access to principal matter. SEC annuity guide Rental property Collect rent after operating costs. Gross rental yield excludes maintenance, vacancies, financing and taxes. Management is work, whether you do it or pay someone else. Dividend funds Distribute cash from stock holdings. Dividends can be cut. A high yield alone says little about future total return or retirement safety. Social Security Provide benefits if your work record qualifies. SSA estimated an average retired-worker benefit of $2,071 a month for January 2026. Your record and claiming age determine yours. SSA estimate Social Security needs its own timeline. You can generally claim retirement benefits from 62; full retirement age is 67 for people born in 1960 or later. Stopping work early can lower benefits because the calculation uses your highest thirty-five years of earnings, including zeros when you have fewer. Check an estimate with future earnings set to your actual plan. The calculator above leaves benefits out rather than treating them as money available today. SSA claiming ages SSA stopping work 09

sections.head: What the projection leaves out
sections.text: Start with the risks that would force a change in spending. Wall Street, October 24, 1929. Associated Press photograph. Public domain .

sections.head: Losses near retirement
sections.text: Sequence risk means that returns arrive in an order that harms a withdrawing portfolio. Selling shares after early losses leaves fewer shares to recover, even when the long-run average return looks acceptable. Cash and bonds, a lower initial withdrawal or spending adjustments can reduce the pressure, but none makes a stock portfolio certain. Bengen's paper began by showing why averages alone were insufficient. Bengen 1994 Decide which expenses you could reduce before testing a flexible withdrawal policy. Skipping an inflation increase is a real spending cut when prices rise. A method that succeeds by reducing spending may fail your personal minimum budget.

sections.head: Inflation and fees
sections.text: At an assumed 3% annual inflation rate, $2.5 million in today's buying power corresponds to about $5.23 million twenty-five years from now. That is calculated compounding, not an inflation forecast. The calculator holds real income and spending constant, so the nominal dollars saved must rise too. Wage growth does not necessarily keep up.

sections.head: Health insurance before Medicare
sections.text: Price coverage for your household and ZIP code before leaving employer insurance. Include premiums, the plan's out-of-pocket limit and expenses outside covered services. Medicare generally begins at 65, and it has premiums and coverage gaps of its own. A national premium estimate cannot price your retirement. Medicare eligibility For 2026, Marketplace premium tax credits generally require household income from 100% through 400% of the applicable poverty guideline, along with other eligibility conditions. For a two-person household in the contiguous states and DC, 2026 coverage uses the 2025 guideline of $21,150, giving an upper income limit of $84,600. Alaska and Hawaii differ. A couple with $85,000 of Marketplace income is over that limit; $60,000 may qualify, but the subsidy amount depends on local benchmark premiums and eligibility. IRS premium tax credit FAQ HealthCare.gov guidelines Marketplace income is modified adjusted gross income, rather than taxable income after the standard deduction. Capital gains, taxable conversions and tax-exempt interest count; wealth itself is not the eligibility test. Affordable employer coverage or Medicare eligibility can disqualify you. From tax year 2026, excess advance premium credits have no repayment cap, making accurate income estimates especially consequential. HealthCare.gov income IRS eligibility and repayment

sections.head: Changes in the household
sections.text: A child, separation, disability or caring for a parent can change both spending and earning capacity. Rather than assigning each a national dollar cost, rerun the budget with the obligations you could face. Insurance and cash reserves protect some risks; a retirement date that assumes uninterrupted work still needs a fallback.

sections.head: Promises of effortless income
sections.text: In its 2024 case against Ascend Ecom, the FTC alleged at least $25 million in losses from an online-storefront scheme marketed with AI and passive-income claims. Scrutinize the return guarantee and what the automation actually does. FTC complaint announcement 10

sections.head: What an investment return represents
sections.text: The portfolio owns claims on businesses and borrowers. Powerhouse mechanic, Lewis Hine, 1920. National Archives, public domain . Shareholders receive dividends and may sell their ownership claims at a different price. Bondholders receive promised interest and principal, subject to the issuer's ability to pay. Workers and productive businesses make those claims valuable, but investors also face competition, failure and changes in what buyers will pay. An index fund spreads ownership across many securities; it cannot fix the return in advance. The businesses and borrowers you hold affect expected return and risk. Choosing that allocation sits between the spending calculation and a usable retirement plan. 11

sections.head: Where the idea came from
sections.text: A short reference, separate from the calculation. Dominguez and the early-retirement idea Joe Dominguez retired from Wall Street work in 1969 at 31 with $70,000 saved. PBS's profile describes his thirty-year approach: live on the interest, keep expenses low and volunteer. He and Vicki Robin later wrote Your Money or Your Life . His Treasury-based plan differs from the stock-and-bond withdrawal research and from the calculator here. PBS profile 12

sections.head: What to check next
sections.text: Turn the estimate into a budget you can test. Use a year's actual spending, including annual bills and repairs, to set a retirement budget. Add the taxes and insurance that would replace payroll deductions. List investable assets separately from housing, reserves and debts. Check when each account can fund spending. Compare more than one return and withdrawal rate. Then test an actual retirement horizon with an allocation-specific withdrawal model. Use your own Social Security estimate and local insurance quote. Revisit both as the planned date gets closer. The calculator can estimate a saving schedule. It cannot determine how much of your spending will be optional after a bad market decade, or how long you will need the portfolio to last.

posts.title: The Third Thing: What We Choose
posts.desc: Genes and upbringing influence a life. Service dogs, twin research and an old court ruling show why that does not settle the question of moral responsibility.

sections.text: Home

sections.head: The Third Thing: What We Choose
sections.text: Genes and upbringing shape a life. A good service dog helps me think about the responsibility we still ask of a person. 8 min essay / Optional source notes scroll Sully served George H. W. Bush before joining the Walter Reed facility-dog program in 2019 . His work is the reason for the dog comparison here. An abused child doesn't have to become an abusive parent. Joan Kaufman and Edward Zigler's 1987 review challenged that expectation. An explanation of how you got here is different from a prediction of everything you'll do next. We inherit tendencies and learn habits before we're old enough to examine them. I think we also have a responsibility to examine them once we can. That's what I mean by the third thing: taking part in the person you're becoming. A well-trained service dog helps me see the distinction, though the dog can only carry the comparison so far. 01

sections.head: What genes can tell us
sections.text: Identical twins raised in different homes can resemble one another on measures of personality, interests and intelligence. Thomas Bouchard and his colleagues' Minnesota study helped establish that inherited differences influence psychological differences. The twins still don't live the same life. The statistic used to describe this is heritability : how much variation in a measured trait, within a particular population and environment, is associated with genetic variation. It doesn't tell you what fraction of a person was made by genes. Nor does a highly heritable trait have to be impossible to change. Twins share much more than a resemblance. Similarities on psychological tests still do not amount to identical lives. Upbringing is also bigger than a parenting style. Two children in one home can have different friends, illnesses, chance encounters and relationships with their parents. Researchers call experiences that make siblings different nonshared environment . Estimates of that component can also include measurement error. The part a study hasn't explained is not a measured quantity of free will. Even Bouchard's paper cautions against treating heritability as a reason to dismiss parenting and education. Finding a small effect of shared upbringing in that sample does not tell us what would happen if a child were denied safety, food or schooling. 02

sections.head: What the dog reveals
sections.text: A service dog makes inherited tendencies and learned behavior visible together. At The Seeing Eye , prospective breeding dogs receive guide-dog training and are selected for health and behavior. Their puppies then live with raisers who teach basic obedience and introduce them to ordinary life before formal training. Selecting parents does not finish the job. Breed is a particularly rough guide to the individual. In Kathleen Morrill and colleagues' 2022 study , breed explained about 9 percent of variation across the surveyed behaviors in the confirmed-purebred analysis. This compares differences among dogs; it does not mean that breeding causes only 9 percent of one dog's behavior. The measures came from owners, whose expectations about breeds can affect their answers. A German Shepherd in a service vest. A breed can suggest tendencies; a working dog still has to be assessed as an individual. Early experience matters, too. The American Veterinary Society of Animal Behavior identifies the first three months as the most important period for socialization, meaning safe exposure to unfamiliar people, animals and places. It also recommends continuing afterward. A missed early opportunity can raise the risk of fear and behavior problems. It doesn't make later learning impossible. An assistance puppy learning to settle on a train. Early socialization matters, and learning continues afterward. What I love in a good service dog is its steadiness. Breeding and training help make that possible. Dogs also learn, solve problems and make decisions. Appreciating Sully doesn't require denying that ordinary sense of choice. The difference I care about is moral accountability. We don't ask Sully to explain why helping a stranger is right, or to reconsider a principle when it harms someone. We ask that of people. That distinction concerns responsibility, not an extra biological ingredient these studies have detected. 03

sections.head: Character takes practice
sections.text: Suppose a wrapper misses the trash can in an empty parking lot. Going back for it is an ordinary decision, with no audience and little reward. It gives you one chance to do what you already think is right. Picking up litter is a small example of doing something because you think you should. Aristotle, in Book II of the Nicomachean Ethics , argues that we become just by doing just acts. He also makes a distinction the habit slogan can miss: an act done accidentally or under instruction is different from an act understood and chosen for its own sake. Repetition matters, but so does the reason for repeating it. That is a useful account of responsibility even if our choices have causes. You don't need to settle the metaphysics of free will before correcting a lie or apologizing for an outburst. Reflection, practice and help from other people are among the ways a life changes. I think a good life asks for this kind of effort. Sometimes it means resisting comfort; sometimes it means accepting care instead of treating suffering as an achievement. The difficult option is not automatically the decent one. Picking up the wrapper is right because the litter shouldn't be left there, not because walking back is unpleasant. 04

sections.head: Pain can prompt change
sections.text: Pain can make an old way of living harder to defend. I think that's one reason the story of a person turning their life around has such force. But I can't turn that judgment into a rule that almost nobody changes while life is comfortable. Learning from someone else, becoming responsible for a child, or finally having a safe place to live can also give someone a reason to change. In Romans 5:3-5 , Paul connects suffering with perseverance, character and hope. His hope rests on God's love. That is a Christian account of suffering, not a psychological guarantee that a painful experience will improve you. Psychologists use post-traumatic growth for positive changes people report after struggling with a crisis. Patricia Frazier and colleagues followed students from before to after distressing events. Students' later reports of growth generally did not match changes on questionnaires taken before and after the event. Some scores did improve. Remembering growth and measuring a change over time are different claims. Cathy Spatz Widom and colleagues' long follow-up of childhood maltreatment found that estimates of transmission differed depending on whether they used agency records, parents' reports or their children's reports. Risk can rise without making an outcome inevitable. Those records don't tell us how many people consciously decided to break a cycle, and they don't reduce prevention to strength of will. I don't want a hopeful argument to become another demand placed on someone who has been hurt. Recovery can require safety, treatment and other people's patience. Continuing to struggle does not mean you refused a lesson that someone else managed to learn. 05

sections.head: Risk is not a verdict
sections.text: There is a dangerous step from saying a trait can be inherited to deciding whose children should exist. On May 2, 1927, the Supreme Court upheld Virginia's compulsory-sterilization law in Buck v. Bell . Carrie Buck challenged the order to sterilize her. Only Justice Pierce Butler dissented. Three generations of imbeciles are enough. Oliver Wendell Holmes Jr., Buck v. Bell , 274 U.S. 200, 207 (1927) Holmes's opinion describes Carrie, her mother and her young daughter as intellectually disabled using the language of the eugenics movement. It accepts the judgment that Carrie was likely to have children deemed socially inadequate. These are the court's assertions. The opinion does not supply reliable genetic evidence for them. The decision is evidence of what a government was willing to do to a person on the strength of those assertions. It is not a study of inheritance. Even a valid estimate of inherited risk would leave the ethical question intact: what could justify taking away this person's reproductive choice? Family history can be relevant when someone thinks about having children. It doesn't establish a person's worth. Nor can this essay promise that every inherited illness or disability will yield to effort. My argument for responsibility has to allow for limits on what someone can control. 06

sections.head: What I believe
sections.text: I think there is a moral order to the world, and that what we put into it is not lost. That is a belief. The dog studies don't establish it, and neither do the stories of people who change after suffering. The Bhagavad Gita , 2.47 , gives the version I find most useful: act without demanding the fruits of the action, and don't use uncertainty about the result as a reason for inaction. Krishna is speaking to Arjuna about duty. My application is narrower: doing right needn't come with a promise that life will pay you back. I also believe the possibility of turning toward a better life should remain open to everyone. That doesn't mean everyone has the same practical chance. Poverty, coercion, illness and the availability of help change what a person can do. If I call someone responsible, I owe them some care in judging what was actually within their reach. A black Labrador. I find a good dog easy to love without asking it for a moral explanation. I can't prove that a choice is independent of everything that caused it, or that the universe notices it. The choice still changes what happens to the person on the receiving end.

sections.head: Sources and limits
sections.text: The research supports particular claims about inheritance, learning and risk. The argument about responsibility, and the belief in a moral order, are mine. Read the methods and source notes

sections.head: Inheritance and dogs
sections.text: Bouchard et al. (1990). Full paper , especially the variance model and discussion of twins' contact and rearing environments. Twins were recruited, not randomly assigned to homes. Morrill et al. (2022). Full paper , breed-variance analysis and methods. The result is an average across measured traits, not total genetic influence or a forecast of working-dog success. Bray et al. (2017). Guide-dog study . Associations between maternal care and later outcomes could be confounded by inherited temperament. They don't tell human parents to withhold affection.

sections.head: Abuse and growth
sections.text: Kaufman and Zigler (1987). Literature review . Its transmission estimate combined studies with different samples, definitions and follow-up periods. It was not a census of survivors or their intentions. Widom et al. (2015). Prospective follow-up of documented childhood maltreatment and matched comparisons. Informants and surveillance affect the estimates; an agency report is not a complete measure of abuse. Frazier et al. (2009). Author-uploaded paper . Mostly female undergraduates, a short interval, and self-reported events limit generalization to other trauma survivors.

sections.head: Texts and judgment
sections.text: Aristotle. Nicomachean Ethics , II.1 and II.4 , W. D. Ross translation. Habituation and deliberate action belong to a philosophical account of virtue. Paul. Romans 5:3-5 , World English Bible. Bhagavad Gita. 2.47 , Swami Mukundananda translation and commentary. The essay paraphrases these passages. Buck v. Bell . Original U.S. Reports opinion , pages 205-208. A primary document for the ruling and its rationale, not confirmation of the family's alleged hereditary condition.
